issues: OnboardingTour overlay (data-testid=onboarding-tour) is fixed inset-0 z-[9997] and intercepts pointer events on repeated visits, even when the underlying page is fully rendered. It re-appears after every page.reload() unless the tour-completion localStorage flag is set. Not a bug per se, but it blocks clicks on tabs / header buttons for a testing agent (had to page.evaluate remove the overlay). Consider persisting tour-complete flag across sessions or setting pointer-events:none on the outer wrapper as intended (the inner card should be pointer-events:auto only).

critical_code_review_comments: crisis_commander.py:_sla_due — falls back to 'High' (2h) when priority is missing/unknown. That is a safe default but consider logging a warning so a mis-typed priority (e.g. 'Urgent') doesn't silently take a 2h SLA when a stakeholder expected 1h.

crisis_commander.py:crisis_report_pack — does two `from studio import ...` and `from reports import ...` inside the handler on every request. Small overhead, but move to module-level to avoid repeated import machinery per request and to fail fast on missing deps.

crisis_commander.py:crisis_report_pack — pulls messages up to 1000 and events up to 500 with no pagination guard; for a very long-lived closed case this could produce a heavy PDF and slow response. Consider size cap + explicit truncation notice in the PDF body.

crisis_commander.py:crisis_report_pack — filename slug drops non-ASCII but doesn't include the case title. Not a bug (spec requires ASCII), just a UX nit — downloaded file identifies only by ref, not by incident title.

CyberCrisisCommander.jsx:unread-mentions useEffect — mentions match uses substring role compare `x.role.toLowerCase().includes(myRole)`. With myRole='admin', this would match ANY roster role whose name contains 'admin' (e.g. 'System Admin'). Fine for now, but consider role === myRole or explicit role-mapping to avoid false positives across tenants.

CyberCrisisCommander.jsx:generateReportPack — surfaces server detail via toast which is good; consider a specific error copy for the 403 case ('Operator role required') so viewers aren't confused by a generic 'Unable to generate report pack.'

CyberCrisisCommander.jsx:1274 tab strip — the crisis-warroom-unread badge uses bg-crit + white text. Good contrast; only shown when unreadMentions > 0. No a11y label though — consider aria-label={`${unreadMentions} unread mentions`} for screen readers.

OnboardingTour overlay z-[9997] with fixed inset-0 pointer-events-none is correct in principle, but its inner card DOES intercept pointer events on the whole viewport during test runs (see design_issues). Playbook: dismiss the tour first, or scope the pointer-events:auto to the modal card only.

rca of the issue: No bugs found. All three iter-137 features behave per spec end-to-end: (1) Decision SLA — demo_seed sets decision_due_at on Awaiting-Approval decisions via _sla_due(priority, now); add_action sets it for any new decision_required=true action; message_to_action sets it (High, 2h); UI reads via obligationCountdown() and renders the crit/amber/muted chip on both Decision Room and War Room. (2) Report Pack — crisis_report_pack handler is operator-gated, aggregates case+events+actions+obligations+messages+participants+recovery, builds markdown via studio._report_markdown and PDF via reports._build_pdf, returns StreamingResponse with ASCII filename; UI button crisis-report-pack-btn is conditionally rendered on selectedCase.status === 'Closed'. (3) Unread @mentions — useEffect polls /messages every 15s, counts messages that mention user by name OR role-substring since localStorage['crisis-warroom-seen-<ref>'] timestamp; opening the War Room tab immediately writes the seen timestamp and sets unreadMentions=0. Badge only renders when count > 0.
